questions.q: How does a social business handle the profit it makes?
a: It repays investors only what they put in and reinvests the rest
It pays investors a growing dividend each year
It relies on grants and donations to keep running
It gives its products away without charging anything
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that investors get back only their original investment, while extra profit goes back into pursuing the social goal.

questions.q: In a type II social business, who owns the company?
a: Poor people
Outside investors
The government
A charitable foundation
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a type II social business is owned by poor people, so its profits work toward reducing poverty.

questions.q: When starting a social business, what should you choose first?
a: One social problem your skills can best address
The largest possible group of investors
A full team of employees to hire
A proven non-profit's operating model
questions.why: Lesson 2 advises picking a single social issue where your own experience gives you the best chance of making a difference.

questions.q: What should a social business's budget show, according to Yunus?
a: Revenue that covers all costs and a rainy day
The lowest possible prices for customers
A yearly share of profits for investors
Dependence on government grants and charity
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the budget must cover every cost plus a reserve, because the business has to sustain itself like a for-profit.

questions.q: Why does the summary call capitalism as we know it incomplete?
a: It has left many people poor while others grew wealthy
It discourages competition and new ideas
It makes companies dependent on donations
It ignores the need to earn a profit
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the gains of modern capitalism were unevenly spread, leaving many people behind in poverty.
